Input Text: During the weekly project meeting, the team agreed that the reporting dashboard cannot launch until the finance data mapping is confirmed. Maya will review the account categories, and Jordan will validate the sample export. No final date was set, but the sponsor asked for an update before Friday. The project manager needs action items and risks without inventing deadlines that were not stated.
Expected Behavior: Extract Maya and Jordan as owners; note Friday update request; do not invent a due date for validation; flag dashboard launch as blocked
Target Format: Action table: Decision/Issue | Owner | Due Date | Risk | Next Step
Risk to Watch: Invented due date; missed blocked-launch risk

Input Text: The operations team discussed a delay in onboarding new vendors because the contract approval queue is backed up. Legal has approved the standard terms, but procurement still needs insurance documents from four vendors. The director asked whether temporary manual approval is possible for low-risk vendors. The team needs a summary of decisions, open questions, and next steps.
Expected Behavior: Identify approved terms and missing insurance docs; flag manual approval as an open question — not a decision; do not state it was approved
Target Format: Action table with open question row
Risk to Watch: Treating open question as a decision; missing insurance doc detail

Input Text: A process review found that customer escalations are being tracked in three separate spreadsheets. Support uses one file, account management uses another, and leadership receives a manually combined version each Friday. The analyst recommended moving to a shared tracker with required fields for owner, status, and next action. The VP needs a summary of the operational problem and recommendation.
Expected Behavior: Summarize fragmented tracking as the core issue; include analyst recommendation; do not overengineer or add steps not mentioned

Input Text: The implementation team completed the first phase of the rollout, but training attendance was lower than expected. Only 58 percent of users attended the live session, and several managers asked for recordings. The help desk also reported repeated questions about login steps. The project sponsor needs a short risk summary and a mitigation plan.
Expected Behavior: Identify low attendance and login questions as risks; recommend recordings and job aids; do not invent attendance target
Target Format: Action table with risk and mitigation
Risk to Watch: Missing training risk linkage; inventing attendance benchmark

Input Text: A vendor demo showed that the automation tool can process invoices faster, but it struggled with handwritten notes and nonstandard purchase order formats. Finance liked the speed improvement but worried about exception handling. The project team needs a balanced summary that avoids presenting the tool as fully ready for production.
Expected Behavior: Present both pros and limitations; recommend pilot or exception handling process; do not state tool is production-ready
Target Format: Action table with balanced assessment row
Risk to Watch: Overstating readiness; missing exception handling concern

Input Text: The monthly operations report shows that average response time improved, but customer satisfaction dropped slightly. The notes indicate that agents are closing tickets faster but customers are reopening more cases for incomplete answers. The director needs a summary that explains why speed alone may not represent better service.
Expected Behavior: Connect faster closure to reopen rate as a quality risk; recommend adding a quality or completeness metric; do not report speed as a pure win
Risk to Watch: Misleading KPI interpretation; missing quality-metric recommendation

Input Text: The team agreed to standardize the intake form, but two departments requested additional custom fields. The project lead warned that too many custom fields may reduce adoption. The executive sponsor asked for a recommendation that balances consistency with department needs. The team needs a decision memo summary.
Expected Behavior: Capture standardization decision and custom-field risk; present adoption concern; do not choose a side not stated in input
Risk to Watch: Missing adoption risk; imposing a resolution not stated

Input Text: A pilot program reduced manual data entry by 30 percent, but the savings depended on employees using the new template correctly. Three teams skipped required fields, which caused rework during reporting. The operations manager needs a summary of results, dependency, and training need.
Expected Behavior: State 30% reduction with dependency caveat; identify skipped fields as training gap; do not present result as unconditional success
Risk to Watch: Ignoring template compliance dependency; missing training action

Input Text: The service team is considering extending support hours during a product launch. Historical data shows call volume increases for two weeks after launch, but staffing overtime has already exceeded budget. The manager asked for a summary of the decision factors and risks.
Expected Behavior: Summarize volume vs. budget tension; present options without choosing one not supported by input; do not recommend a specific staffing model
Target Format: Action table with open decision row
Risk to Watch: Unsupported staffing recommendation; missing budget constraint

Input Text: A cross-functional meeting identified confusion about who approves customer credits above $500. Sales thought finance owned the decision, while finance said account management must approve the customer relationship impact first. The team needs a summary that identifies the ownership gap and recommends a clearer workflow.
Expected Behavior: Identify ownership gap clearly; recommend approval matrix or workflow; include both stakeholder views
Risk to Watch: Missing one stakeholder view; inventing an approval owner
